mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive when unemployment is below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts and consumer spending indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive when both proxies increase.

mechanism_narrative: During easing, lower federal funds rate stimulates equity markets, leading to positive returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive when FEDFUNDS is below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth indicates strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive when industrial production grows.

mechanism_narrative: CPI above 325 indicates inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not negative when CPI exceeds 325.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment and low unemployment indicate economic strength, leading to positive returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive when both employment and low unemployment occur.

mechanism_narrative: During expansion, rising housing starts indicate growth, leading to positive returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive when housing starts exceed 1300.
